conventions.convention: All spaces are nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. Matrix logarithms are defined spectrally; the reference state is strictly positive.

Entropy and relative entropy use natural logarithms, with zero-eigenvalue entropy contribution 0 log 0 := 0; entropy is in nats. K_sigma := -log sigma is modular data, without an asserted physical-energy interpretation.

The matrix-entropy derivative requires real and imaginary entries differentiable at the specified interior point and positive-definite self-adjoint matrices on a neighborhood; commutativity of the path is not assumed.

The density path is entrywise C1 on an open interval containing zero, has trace one throughout, and passes through a faithful reference. The stated relative-entropy derivative clause additionally assumes entrywise C2.
For the two-level example, 0 < p < 1 and |epsilon| < min(p, 1-p); the interval excludes singular endpoints.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated finite-dimensional path A, entrywise differentiable at t0 and self-adjoint positive definite near t0, G(t) := tr(A(t) log A(t)) is differentiable at t0 and G'(t0) = tr(A'(t0)(log A(t0) + I_H)).

For finite-dimensional density operators rho, sigma with sigma strictly positive, D(rho||sigma) = Delta_K(rho,sigma) - (s(rho)-s(sigma)), where K_sigma := -log sigma and Delta_K := tr((rho-sigma)K_sigma). For a nonzero finite tensor factorization, D(Tr_B rho||Tr_B sigma) ≤ D(rho||sigma).

For the stated entrywise C1 density path through a faithful finite-dimensional reference sigma, d s(rho(epsilon))/d epsilon at zero equals tr(rho'(0)K_sigma). If the path is additionally entrywise C2, D(rho(epsilon)||sigma) has zero first derivative at zero.

Product and quotient logarithm identities and log 1 = 0.
Geometric convergence and evaluation for ratios of absolute value less than one.
Scalar logarithm-series derivation and convergence of differentiated geometric sums.
Identification of the scalar power series with -log(1-x) on (-1,1).

Support convention and trace formula for finite quantum relative entropy.
Natural-log spectral entropy with zero-eigenvalue contribution zero.
Contraction of the second tensor factor in ordered product coordinates.
Relative entropy cannot increase under tracing out a nonzero finite tensor factor.
Sum and product differentiation in the explicit two-level calculation.
